structured_output.world_model:
W1 (mechanism), after E008.

The setup
- The tip code reads epochs=9.5 at batch 2000: 25 steps per epoch, 238 steps in total. The idea texts' epoch labels look about one epoch behind the code ("9→8.5" was really 10→9.5).
- Resolution switches are now keyed on step fraction: 40% of steps at 24 px, 30% at 28 px, 30% at 32 px.
- The pixel-weighted cost is 0.755 of full resolution.

Measured effects
- Compile + fused SGD: about −14% time, same math (E002→E004). E003 and E004 gave identical accuracy (0.748633), so compiled training looks deterministic per seed. Re-run noise is then mostly zero for accuracy and about 1-2% for time.
- Lookahead/EMA: +0.97 pp for about 0.6% time (E005).
  - The t^3 alpha ramp averages the late high-lr iterates, including the BN buffers.
  - It acts as a strong anneal, worth about 1.5 epochs.
- Muon on the conv filters: +0.66 pp at about +4% time (E006).
  - Orthogonalized updates on fixed-norm filters give a better step per sample at batch 2000.
- Progressive resizing: −22% time, −0.59 pp (E007).
  - Measured time tracks the pixel share (0.776 vs 0.755), so the run is GPU/FLOP-bound.
- Epoch slope with EMA and Muon on: a 0.5-epoch cut gave −0.18 pp and −4.8% time (E007→E008). This sits at the low end of my 0.25-0.35 pp per 0.5 epoch expectation, so the recipe is fairly flat near here.

The time model
- Fixed cost is about 0.4 s (H2D copy, eigh, pad, per-epoch augment/interpolate).
- Per-step cost is about 27 ms on average and about 35 ms at 32 px.
- FLOP shares by group are about 20/50/32%. The last group works on small spatial maps, so narrowing it 576→512 saves about 3% of time.
- CPU launch overhead is small at 2000-sample steps, so CUDA graphs can gain only a few percent. They also risk the Lookahead/Muon state living outside the graph.

The accuracy model
- Margin left: 0.42 pp, worth about 1 epoch at the current slope, or one more resizing notch.
- Lowering the LR floor to 0 overlaps with EMA. I expect +0.1-0.2 pp, not ≥0.3.
- BN recompute duplicates the EMA buffer averaging. I expect ≤0.15 pp gain, plus a new-shape autotune cost.
- Moving to 20 px:
  - the group-3 maps shrink to 2×2;
  - 30% of steps at 20 px is a big information cut.
  I expect −0.5 to −0.9 pp.

Noise
- The 3-seed mean std is about 0.15-0.2 pp from seed variance.
- Keep the 3-seed mean at 0.755 or above for 40-seed safety.

Unsure
- Epoch labeling in the idea texts versus the code.
- Whether the slope stays as flat as E008 suggests: is −0.18 pp per 0.5 epoch real or noise?
- How much the 20 px phase damages accuracy when EMA covers only the 32 px tail.

forecasts.reason: EMA already anneals the endpoint, so a zero floor adds only about +0.15 pp. That is within noise and below the 0.3 pp threshold.
Pixel share drops from 0.755 to 0.639, about −13% time. The 20 px phase costs about 0.7 pp, roughly what 1 epoch would, so it is a wash and likely below the bar.
Group 3 runs on tiny spatial maps, so the saving is only about 3%, under the 4% threshold. The accuracy loss is about 0.2 pp.
Held-out seeds should land within 0.3 pp of the seeds 0-2 mean with a std of about 0.2-0.3 pp. Build warms every shape, so the first epoch's overhead should be small.
Steps are GPU-bound at batch 2000, so the launch overhead to remove is small, and the Lookahead/Muon state outside the graph adds copies. I expect a gain under 3%, with some risk of breakage.
The EMA already averages the BN buffers, so the gain is about +0.05 pp. The new 5k batch shape adds cuDNN autotune and forward time of about 0.15 s or more.

cruxes: Is the epoch slope really as flat as E008 suggests (−0.18 pp per 0.5 epoch)? If so, cutting epochs to 8.5-9 on the code's scale beats more aggressive resizing.
How much accuracy does a 20 px phase cost when EMA covers only the 32 px tail? This decides whether I011 can clear 0.753.
Does an accuracy-buying change (LR to 0, or an LS/lr retune) yield ≥0.2 pp that can be spent on a further 0.5-epoch cut at no time cost?
